vjimc-1995-cat1-01.prompt:
Discuss the solvability of the system of equations
$$\begin{aligned}\lambda x + y + z &= a\\ x + \lambda y + z &= b\\ x + y + \lambda z &= c\end{aligned}$$
for all numbers $\lambda, a, b, c \in \mathbb R$.
vjimc-1995-cat1-01.answer: For $\lambda\notin\{1,-2\}$ there is exactly one solution, $x=\frac{(\lambda+1)a-b-c}{(\lambda-1)(\lambda+2)}$ (and cyclically); for $\lambda=1$ it is solvable iff $a=b=c$ (two-parameter family); for $\lambda=-2$ it is solvable iff $a+b+c=0$ (one-parameter family). The determinant is $(\lambda-1)^2(\lambda+2)$.

vjimc-1995-cat1-02.prompt: Let $f(x)$ be an even twice differentiable function such that $f''(0)\neq 0$. Prove that $f(x)$ has a local extremum at $x=0$.
vjimc-1995-cat1-02.answer: Evenness forces $f'(0)=0$ (the one-sided difference quotients are negatives of each other); then $f''(0)\ne0$ and the second-derivative test give a strict local extremum.
